correctness.rationale: For \(K\) algebraically closed of characteristic \(2\), the four first partials of \(e_3\) satisfy \(f_4=f_1+f_2+f_3\), while Euler's identity gives \(e_3\) in the gradient ideal because \(3=1\). Xie's dimension formula gives dimension \(1\) in the \((n,d,p)=(4,3,2)\) case, so the three quadratic generators form a height-three complete intersection of degree \(8\). Xie's local-ring theorem gives generic multiplicity \(2\) on each of the four coordinate-axis components, already accounting for total degree \(8\). The bundled exact checker independently verifies the stronger ideal identity \(I=Q_1\cap Q_2\cap Q_3\cap Q_4\) by Buchberger reduction and elimination over \(\mathbf F_2\). Each quotient \(R/Q_i\) is \(K[x_i,t]/(t^2)\), so \(Q_i\) is primary to the corresponding axis prime; complete-intersection unmixedness excludes embedded primes.
